stages.title: Line bundles and the graded algebra
stages.description:
## RF3. Line bundles and the graded algebra

Define O(1) by Frobenius descent with the chosen pi-normalization; construct O(n), tensor
and dual comparisons, divisor sections and transition functions. Prove the sign conversion
between Frobenius eigenvalue and degree. Form the graded algebra of global sections for
affinoid S and construct Proj and the analytic-to-schematic map of locally ringed spaces.
The ampleness/GAGA theorem belongs to VectorBundlesAndIsocrystals VB2; this stage owns
the graded algebra, map and restriction identifications it uses.

stages.title: Patching and modifications
stages.description: ## RF4. Patching and modifications ### RF4:vector-bundles — Linear patching Prove Beauville–Laszlo gluing for finite locally free modules along the Cartier divisors just constructed: a bundle off D, a bundle on its formal neighborhood, and an isomorphism on the punctured neighborhood determine a bundle, with a fully faithful and essentially surjective gluing functor. Prove compatibility with tensor, dual, base change and several disjoint divisors. For nonnoetherian coefficient rings retain completeness, Cartier and finite-projectivity hypotheses in the algebraic patching argument. ### RF4:G-torsors — Tannakian transfer Transfer the preceding gluing to G-torsors via the exact tensor-functor comparison supplied in BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0. BG0 only imports RF0–RF3 and VB1, not this return. Prove independence of faithful representation and compatibility with extension of structure group; only then export the modification interpretation to GS0/BG2.

stages.title: Tannakian transfer
stages.description:
### RF4:G-torsors — Tannakian transfer

Transfer the preceding gluing to G-torsors via the exact tensor-functor comparison
supplied in BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0. BG0 only imports RF0–RF3 and VB1, not this
return. Prove independence of faithful representation and compatibility with extension
of structure group; only then export the modification interpretation to GS0/BG2.

stages.title: Linear patching
stages.description: ### RF4:vector-bundles — Linear patching Prove Beauville–Laszlo gluing for finite locally free modules along the Cartier divisors just constructed: a bundle off D, a bundle on its formal neighborhood, and an isomorphism on the punctured neighborhood determine a bundle, with a fully faithful and essentially surjective gluing functor. Prove compatibility with tensor, dual, base change and several disjoint divisors. For nonnoetherian coefficient rings retain completeness, Cartier and finite-projectivity hypotheses in the algebraic patching argument.

stages.title: Artin v-stacks and eligible operations
stages.description:
## VS0. Artin v-stacks and eligible operations

Define Artin v-stacks by representable diagonals and the cohomologically smooth atlas
condition of FS IV.1; prove atlas independence and stability under fibre products.
Construct smooth-lisse descent of the enhanced coefficient category and extend the
allowed operations with specified representability, separation and finite-dimensional
hypotheses. Prove pullback, exceptional pullback and their normalization for smooth
atlases, and the comparison with existing small-v-stack ECD categories.

Construct partial compact-support functors of FS IV.5 for stacks whose structural map
is not in the original representable ECD class. Prove independence of presentation,
adjunctions and base-change formulas in their actual scope. In particular notation
pi-sharp for an Artin stack is not an unqualified ordinary ECD Rpi!.

stages.title: ULA, Jacobian criterion and localization
stages.description:
## VS1. ULA, Jacobian criterion and localization

Define relative local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity with the overconvergence,
geometric-fibre and constructibility conditions of FS IV.2. Prove base change, composition,
descent, tensor and relative-dual properties with all compactness hypotheses. Construct
formal smoothness and the Jacobian criterion of IV.3–IV.4 for the specified relative
section functors on Fargues–Fontaine curves. Prove the tangent/cohomology calculation,
the positive-slope condition and the resulting cohomological smoothness. This general
criterion uses already established diamond geometry; it cannot justify the earlier
AdicEtaleGeometry A3 input to constructing diamonds.

Construct attractor/repeller correspondences, hyperbolic localization and the comparison
map of FS IV.6, including equivariance and boundedness hypotheses. Prove its compatibility
with base change and duality. Establish Drinfeld's lemma IV.7 for the divisor/Weil-action
applications, separating partial Frobenius descent from an arbitrary fundamental-group
product claim. Satake uses these results as named inputs.

stages.title: Condensed and solid foundations
stages.description:
## VS2. Condensed and solid foundations

Use Mathlib's `CondensedMod`, its free/forgetful adjunction, and its profinite free-module
and solidification maps. The current `CondensedMod.IsSolid` documentation explicitly
restricts its naive general-ring definition: first prove the finite-type Z-algebra
construction, then extend to general coefficient rings by the prescribed restriction
of scalars. Do not silently use that predicate as already correct for every ring.
Construct the missing solidification universal property, derived solid
tensor/Hom and the generators/exactness needed for FS VII.1. Build the finite/cofiltered
limit and completion comparisons with actual topological modules. These are new module
constructions on EnhancedDerivedSheaves' common enhancement, not a second infinity model.

Construct D_solid(X,Lambda) over the appropriate cutoffs on a small v-stack, four
operations and relative homology f-sharp in the FS VII.2–VII.3 range. Prove the solid
projection/base-change identities, comparison with torsion D_et, and dualizability theorem
of VII.4–VII.5. The unrestricted large solid category need not be presentable at one
fixed universe; construct compatible adjoints at adequate cutoffs.

stages.title: Lisse categories and coefficients
stages.description:
## VS3. Lisse categories and coefficients

Fix ell != p and a discrete Z_ell-algebra Lambda, interpreted as the condensed extension
Z_ell tensor_(Z_ell,disc) Lambda_disc. Define D_lis of an Artin v-stack as the stable
subcategory closed under sums generated by f-sharp Lambda for separated maps f
representable in locally spatial diamonds and ell-cohomologically smooth. Here lisse refers to the Artin-stack lisse site, not to
the assertion that every object is a locally constant local system.

Prove the inclusion's right adjoint, tensor closure, pullback and lisse internal Hom/
pushforward constructions. Compare ordinary, adic, solid and lisse coefficients through
the actual fully faithful functors of VII.6. Prove reduction and scalar extension in
their established range. Rational coefficients require the constructed solid/lisse
localization; replacing every integral complex by its tensor with Q_ell is not the
definition of a completed coefficient system.

stages.title: Sheaves on Bun_G strata and compact generation
stages.description:
## VS4. Sheaves on Bun_G strata and compact generation

Identify D_et([*/H],Lambda) with the enhanced derived category of smooth H-representations
for H locally pro-p and prime-to-p torsion Lambda. Construct both functors using continuous
torsor descent; identify pullback with forgetting the action and invariants with the
derived appropriate pushforward. Apply this to J_b(E), and prove the connected-kernel
invariance giving the category for nonbasic Bun_G^b. Extend to D_lis in the precise
coefficient range of VII.7.

Prove localization triangles and the infinite semiorthogonal decomposition along the
HN strata using justified exhaustions. Characterize compact objects by compact restrictions
with finite stratum support, and by the thick closure of compact induction from pro-p
open subgroups. These are the same compact induction objects as the local-group roadmap.

stages.title: Duality and admissible objects
stages.description:
## VS5. Duality and admissible objects

Construct Bernstein–Zelevinsky duality on compact Bun_G objects using the partial-support
functor; prove biduality and its basic-stratum comparison. Separately construct Verdier
duality on ULA objects and prove that ULA is equivalent to perfection of K-invariants on
every stratum for every appropriate pro-p open K. Prove scalar-extension and Hecke-use
compatibility; admissibility of complexes means perfect invariants, not just finite
dimensions of separate cohomology groups.

stages.title: Isocrystals and slope conventions
stages.description:
## VB0. Isocrystals and slope conventions

For E-breve with its q-Frobenius sigma, construct finite-dimensional spaces with a
bijective sigma-semilinear operator, their morphisms, exact tensor category and descent.
Prove the Dieudonné–Manin classification after the stipulated algebraically closed residue
base, including simple objects of rational slope, multiplicities, Hom and endomorphism
division algebras. Use the campaign's Brauer/local-field theory for the invariant and
prove its compatibility with the explicit cyclic algebra; absent such an input, the
cyclic-algebra and Brauer-invariant calculation is an obligation here.

Pin the convention by the standard rank-r block with Frobenius r-th power pi^s sigma^r.
Compute the slope of its associated bundle and record any sign reversal explicitly.
Prove functoriality under coefficient extension, tensor slope addition and dual slope
negation. A classification after algebraic closure is not a classification of all
descent forms over an arbitrary perfectoid field.

stages.title: Vector bundles, descent and cohomology
stages.description:
## VB1. Vector bundles, descent and cohomology

Define bundles as finite locally free O_X modules on the existing curve; compare with
finite projective modules on annuli and Frobenius descent. Prove rational/pro-étale/v
descent in the exact source scope, effective gluing and preservation of tensor, Hom and
duals. Construct the isocrystal-to-bundle functor and natural comparison under S-base change.

Build degree, rank, slope, saturated subbundles and semistability, including exact-sequence
degree additivity and the behavior of torsion quotients. Construct H^0 and H^1 and prove
higher vanishing for bundles in the stipulated affinoid-relative setting. Compute O(n)
sections and first cohomology with actual Frobenius maps and signs. The curve need not be
proper over an adic field for these formulas; establish them from annular descent.

stages.title: Ampleness, algebraization and geometric classification
stages.description: ## VB2. Ampleness, algebraization and geometric classification ### VB2:ampleness — Positive twists and algebraization For affinoid perfectoid S prove that sufficiently positive twists of a bundle are globally generated with higher cohomology zero. Compare bundles and cohomology on X_S and the Proj curve built in RF3. For S a geometric perfectoid point, prove regular noetherian dimension-one structure of the schematic curve, its local principal-ideal properties and the closed-point description under the source's hypotheses. This stage uses RF3 and VB1, not projectivized-section properness or classification. ### VB2:classification — Geometric points Prove that every bundle at a geometric point is a direct sum of the stable O(lambda) and that these stable bundles have the ranks and degrees prescribed by reduced rational slopes. The isocrystal functor induces the source's bijection on isomorphism classes; it is not asserted fully faithful onto all bundle morphisms. Prove Hom/Ext vanishing, extension and uniqueness properties needed for HN filtrations and moduli charts.

stages.description: ## VB3. Banach–Colmez geometry without circular classification ### VB3:positive-basic-examples — The independent local calculation Construct the sheaf of sections T ↦ H^0(X_T,E_T), beginning with the explicit positive line-bundle and Lubin–Tate universal-cover calculations used in the proof of VB2. Prove diamond representability, local spatiality and exact-sequence behavior by those calculations and v-descent. Negative H^1 spaces have their separate construction. Use FS II.2.1's Lubin–Tate calculation and II.2.15's endomorphism analysis as the positive/basic input to VB2:classification, alongside VB2:ampleness and the Hom/Ext calculations. Do not use classification to prove its own positive-section input. ### VB3:projectivized-properness — The input to families Prove II.2.16's properness of `(BC(E)\{0})/E×` using II.2.6 ampleness and II.2.5(iii); the properness proof is independent of geometric classification. Its consumer is VB4's relative HN/nowhere-vanishing-section argument (II.2.19), not VB2:classification. Construct projectivization with scalar action and prove the properness and v-cover properties used to produce nowhere-zero sections. State the slope bounds in perfectoid-open-ball identifications; not every Banach–Colmez space is representable by a perfectoid space.

stages.title: Families and HN strata
stages.description:
## VB4. Families and HN strata

Inputs: VB2:classification, VB3:projectivized-properness and VB1. The construction
of nowhere-vanishing sections after a v-cover uses the **proper** projectivized
section space; neither a pointwise classification nor mere surjectivity supplies it.

Construct the geometric HN polygon of E_s, prove its semicontinuity with the source's
dominance convention, and prove existence of the relative HN filtration on constant-polygon
loci. Show that constant-slope pieces become sums of O(lambda) pro-étale locally under
the precise source assumptions. Prove the equivalence between everywhere slope-zero
bundles and pro-étale E-local systems, with tensor and scalar-extension compatibility.
Keep local systems distinct from trivial constant bundles; the descent datum is essential.
